title: Clipboard and bounded network MCP exposure
objective: Expose only the already-qualified bounded clipboard and destination-scoped network shapes as static reviewed MCP tools: one explicit clipboard read sample and one explicit clipboard write placement under the closed SG-000038 and SG-000039 secret, sequence, bound, and per-operation approval controls, and one HTTPS fetch of a public destination under the closed SG-000040 SSRF, address-set binding, redirect, bound, and approval controls; qualify each against its live native implementation first, and preserve the clipboard surveillance, paste, generic socket, proxy, and unrestricted fetch denials.

include: a live qualification of the clipboard read, clipboard write, and network fetch shapes against their native adapters on real Windows before exposure
static MCP tools for one clipboard read sample, one clipboard write placement, and one destination-scoped HTTPS fetch, each forwarding exactly its closed kernel shape with fresh local approval
remote reach decided per tool with a default deny for anything unmapped, and the clipboard kept off every remote path unless a reviewed reason permits it
catalog, scope, parity inventory, release qualification, and client example pins for the new tools
real Windows evidence for clipboard sequence binding, secret denial, and bounds, and test evidence for network SSRF, redirect, and address-set binding
exclude: clipboard monitoring, polling, history, subscriptions, or any standing clipboard session
paste automation or any input, keyboard, or desktop authority from a clipboard write
generic sockets, proxies, tunnels, non-HTTPS schemes, request methods other than the closed fetch, caller headers, or request bodies
any new network destination class beyond the closed public-address HTTPS fetch

authority_delta.network: One approved HTTPS GET to a public destination per call, bound to the approved address set, with same-origin redirects and the closed body bound.
authority_delta.ui_input: None; a clipboard write never pastes or injects input.
authority_delta.secrets: Secret-pattern clipboard content is denied in both directions; responses carry bounded content only.
authority_delta.approval: Fresh per-operation local approval for every clipboard read, clipboard write, and fetch, bound to the exact digest.

invariants: no clipboard surveillance: each approval authorizes at most one read or one write
a clipboard write is never paste or input authority
network reach is destination-scoped HTTPS to validated public addresses only; no generic socket, proxy, or unrestricted fetch exists
no MCP tool claims clipboard or network capability the native implementation does not have

acceptance.claim: Clipboard read and write tools are live on real Windows with sequence binding, secret denial, bounds, and per-operation approval, and never monitor or paste.
The network fetch tool reaches only approved public HTTPS destinations with address-set binding, same-origin bounded redirects, and bounded output, and every generic network shape stays denied.
Exact-head CI, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.sg_000065: Tool profiles and the metadata contract may proceed only after SG-000064 closes.

done_when: Bounded clipboard and destination-scoped network tools are canonical and exposed with their closed controls, and every surveillance, paste, and generic network shape stays denied.

canonical_evidence.jev: PASSED: genuine TypeSafe Jev exact-diff review covered 32/32 hunks with zero findings and zero blocking findings, pin 31f89602797fb7bea007f8a480bf368bf564954e
canonical_evidence.ocr: PASSED: Alibaba Open Code Review v1.12.9 exact-range delegation over 17 changed files, 10 reviewable with delegated rules applied and 7 excluded (apps/cotra-mcp/src/clipboard.test.ts, network.test.ts, oauth-authorization.test.ts, surface.test.ts, and transport-contract.test.ts by default-path classification and docs/p16/CAPABILITY_PARITY.md and docs/security/SG-000064_CLIPBOARD_NETWORK_NOTE.md by unsupported-extension classification) manually reviewed
canonical_evidence.security_review: PASS on exact qualified head: three static MCP tools each forward exactly one closed kernel shape with fresh per-operation local approval: clipboard_read (one Unicode-text sample bound to the pre-approval clipboard sequence, secret, empty, oversized, and changed content refused, no monitoring), clipboard_write (one placement bound to the text digest, secret, empty, and oversized text now refused before the approval prompt and again after approval, never paste or input), and web_fetch (one HTTPS GET to a public destination bound to the approved address set with same-origin bounded redirects and a 1 MiB body, projected to UTF-8 text or binary metadata only); no MCP socket, HTTP client, method, header, or proxy primitive; all three local-only and denied on every remote path. Live real Windows clipboard round trip with stale and secret refusals, a live WinHTTP fetch of a public destination, and always-on refusal of non-HTTPS, loopback, private, metadata, localhost, and userinfo destinations. All closed SG-000001 through SG-000063 regressions pass. CodeRabbit skipped-review and cubic skipping notices evaluated as non-evidence noise with zero substantive findings; zero unresolved threads.
canonical_evidence.authority_boundary: Three local-only MCP tools over the closed SG-000038, SG-000039, and SG-000040 shapes (one approved clipboard read, one approved clipboard write, one approved public HTTPS GET). No clipboard surveillance, paste, input, generic socket, proxy, or remote clipboard or network authority.
